patch.value: Expected revisions advance from the pre-override document when an item_store_write override transforms contents

Found in Codex review round 22 of PR #1654 (pm-gh1576). When a supported item_store_write extension override changes the persisted contents (for example a description-only transform), mutateItem advances the revision scope with its pre-override afterDocument. That hash does not describe the stored item, so a second guarded write in the same withExpectedItemRevisions scope (or a multi-write CLI command such as claim --start) refuses with item_revision_conflict although no other writer ran. It fails closed: a false refusal, never a lost update. advanceItemMutationPreconditions in core/store/item-mutation-precondition.ts receives the document from the item-store write path before the override result is known. Fix direction: advance from the persisted snapshot under the item lock (re-read or the override's returned contents), accounting for overrides that skip the write or delete, or refuse an incompatible override for a guarded write before committing.

A guarded scope that writes the same item twice under a contents-transforming item_store_write override admits both writes; A skipped or delete-converted override write advances the scope to the stored state (or refuses before commit), with a spec for each; A competing peer write between the two guarded writes still refuses with item_revision_conflict
Under a contents-transforming item_store_write override, a guarded scope advances to the revision actually persisted, so its own next write is admitted and only a competing write refuses.
The scope advances to the pre-override document hash, so its own next guarded write refuses with item_revision_conflict.
